correctness.rationale: The exact conditional 11-count distributions from Sobolewski--Spiegelhofer Proposition 3.2 give the initial rational functions A1,B1. The displayed recursions imply B_{2^k-1}=H for k>=3, the rational boundary J=A15, and the polynomial difference K=A31-A15=(z-1)^2(z+1)(2z^2+z+2)/64. Induction shows every later difference is a nonnegative z-power multiple of K; K(1)=0 so it changes no negative coefficient or total mass. The even-shift formula similarly preserves the negative mass for j>=1. Negative Laurent masses 9/32, 27/64, 27/64, 73/64 yield 83/128 and 39/64; direct rational base cases give the remaining six values. The extracted verifier checks these algebraic identities and initial cases with exact fractions, with finite enumeration used only diagnostically.

value.rationale: The original 2023 paper explicitly leaves the strict-density analogue of Cusick open; shifts with a single maximal run constitute a complete natural infinite hard regime outside its many-runs Gaussian approximation. A sharp uniform bound 39/64 for the whole family is meaningful, and the stronger negative-tail invariance once run length exceeds four explains why arbitrarily long blocks produce the same exact probability. This is an infinite structural rigidity, not isolated small-t enumeration or the established recurrence alone.
